newsitem.title: USA: Hundreds of soldiers allowed home after gun search.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds of soldiers allowed home after gun search.

text.p: More than 500 soldiers from the Army's 3rd Infantry Division were allowed to go home Tuesday for the first time in a week after a pair of stolen pistols forced officers to keep them in their barracks area, an Army spokesman said.
But a similar restriction remained in place for another 60 soldiers from an engineering unit after a pair of night-vision goggles disappeared from its cache of equipment.

Fort Benning spokesman Al Blanchard said two 9-mm pistols, found missing March 11 from an armoured regiment of the infantry division, were recovered by the Army investigators late Monday after an anonymous tip.
Between the disappearance of the guns and their recovery, the regiment was restricted to its own area of the 182,000-acre Army post.
"They'll be allowed to go home tonight," Blanchard said after the ban was lifted.

"This is routine business. It's our approach to handling this particular problem, and this time it worked. The weapons were recovered, based on a tip from an anonymous caller. In other words, the guy got sick and tired of being locked up."

The night-vision goggles also were discovered missing March 11 from the division's 317th engineers battalion. The unit's 60 members would remain restricted to their area of the post until the article was recovered, Blanchard said.
Fort Benning houses the 3rd Brigade of the 3rd Infantry Division and the 75th Ranger Regiment, which together encompass about 22,000 soldiers.
